record.context_brief: Hawaii conjecture on real zeros of D(p'/p)
record.original_question:
Let p(x) be a real polynomial of degree n ≥ 2 with exactly 2d nonreal
zeros, where 0 ≤ 2d ≤ n, and define Q(x) =
D(p'/p)(x), where D = d/dx. Must the number Z_R(Q) of real zeros of Q,
counted with multiplicity, satisfy Z_R(Q) ≤ 2d?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p(x)$ be a real polynomial of degree $n \geq 2$, and suppose that $p$ has exactly $2d$ nonreal zeros (counted with multiplicity), where $0 \leq 2d \leq n$. Define
$$Q(x) := D\!\left(\frac{p'}{p}\right)(x), \qquad D := \frac{d}{dx}.$$
Let $Z_{\mathbb{R}}(Q)$ denote the number of real zeros of $Q$, counted with multiplicity. Must one have
$$Z_{\mathbb{R}}(Q) \leq 2d?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Hawaii conjecture was proved by Mikhail Tyaglov in 2009/2011, establishing that the number of real zeros of (p'/p)' does not exceed the number of nonreal zeros of p. Recent works (2024–2025) discuss generalizations and alternative proofs (e.g., via Cauchy indices).

status_evidence.title: On the number of real critical points of logarithmic derivatives and the Hawaii conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Tyaglov establishes a connection leading to a proof of the Hawaii conjecture that the number of real zeros of Q=(φ'/φ)' does not exceed the number of nonreal zeros of φ.
status_evidence.claim: The Hawaii conjecture was proved by M. Tyaglov.

status_evidence.title: Hawaii conjecture through the lens of Cauchy indices
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper revisiting the (proved) Hawaii conjecture using Cauchy indices.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is treated as a known theorem with new proofs/generalizations.
